slides.headline: On September 9th, a college that started with one man's stubborn idea became a university.
The Aligarh Muslim University Act
slides.body: In 1875, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College - a bet that Muslims in India needed modern, Western-style education without giving up their own identity. On September 9, 1920, an Act of the legislature converted it into Aligarh Muslim University.

slides.headline: One founder's idea needed a generation to become an institution.
slides.body: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan didn't live to see the university - he died in 1898. It took the Muslim University Association, founded around 1900, two more decades of fundraising and organizing before the Act finally passed.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Institutions outlive the people who start them.
slides.body: Every college, research lab or training institute being built today is making the same bet Sir Syed made - that education built now pays off for a generation that hasn't been born yet.
